claims.text: Annealed single-phase bcc HfNbTaTiZr can contain a percolated, continuous network of SRO clusters.
Percolation of SRO clusters in bcc HfNbTaTiZr will cause a sharp, nonlinear transition in thermal conductivity.
The percolated state will have substantially lower thermal conductivity than predicted by serial/parallel mixing or point-defect scattering models.
A percolated SRO network creates a continuous, rugged potential-energy surface in HfNbTaTiZr.
The rugged SRO network acts as a phonon glass and increases phonon scattering across a broad frequency spectrum.
Standard SRO transport models treat SRO regions as independent, discrete Rayleigh-scattering centers.
Prior MoNbTaW evidence shows that SRO impedes dislocation motion through a rugged potential-energy landscape.
Potential-energy-surface ruggedness inferred from dislocation mobility can also create a high density of phonon-scattering states.
Correlated chemical fluctuations in a continuous SRO network produce a conductivity reduction exceeding the sum of independent scattering events.
The critical SRO percolation threshold is likely above 15–20 vol%.
Above the threshold, thermal conductivity will fall below 5 W m^-1 K^-1 and below the Cahill–Pohl theoretical minimum or simple mixing-rule predictions.
The percolated state will exhibit weaker temperature dependence of thermal conductivity than a conventional crystal and will approach amorphous-solid behavior.
Serial/parallel mixing, point-defect scattering, and Cahill–Pohl models predict linear or sublinear conductivity reduction with SRO volume fraction.
The proposed mechanism applies only when the alloy remains single-phase bcc and its SRO clusters percolate.
The mechanism does not apply to isolated SRO clusters or to phase-separated precipitates.
The conductivity decrease depends on the phonon mean free path relative to SRO cluster size.
Changing cooling rate can control SRO cluster size and connectivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
APT and high-resolution TEM can quantify SRO cluster size, volume fraction, and the percolation threshold in this alloy.
Absence of a sharp conductivity drop at the measured connectivity threshold, together with agreement with an independent-scattering model, would falsify the proposed percolation mechanism.

contradictions.description: Cahill–Pohl is variously characterized as a point-defect or volume-fraction scattering model and as a theoretical minimum-conductivity model. These are not equivalent baselines, so the proposed quantitative comparison and falsification criterion are internally ambiguous.
